newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says Britain should release funds for medical goods.
newsitem.headline: Court says Britain should release funds for medical goods.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Tuesday the Bank of England should release funds to Centro-Com of Italy to pay for medical goods shipped from Italy to Serbia and Montenegro.

After trade sanctions were imposed on the former Yugoslav states both by the United Nations and the European Union, Britain stopped the release of payment for medical goods shipped there, unless the goods originated in the United Kingdom.

In response to Britain's contention that its banking measures were adopted under its national competence over foreign policy, the court said "member states have indeed retained their competence in the field of foreign and security policy... nonetheless the powers retained must be exercised in a manner consistent with Community law."

The common commercial policy agreed by member states under article 13 of the EEC Treaty, and implemented by Council regulation, prohibits most trade between EU members and the Republics of Serbia and Montenegro.

However, the sanctions regulations allow for the shipment to Serbia and Montenegro of goods certified strictly medical by the United Nations Sanctions Committee, where the exporter has obtained an export permit from the country of origin.
In answer to Britain's claim that to release the funds would violate a prior commitment to non-EU nations, the European court said the national court must determine that issue.

"It should, in any event, be remembered that, when an international agreement allows, but does not require, a member state to adopt a measure contrary to Community law, the member state must refrain from adopting such a measure," the court said.
EXCERPTS FROM THE JUDGMENT
(Original language of the case: English)
"Foreign and security policy - Common commercial policy - Blocking of funds - Sanctions against the Republics of Serbia and Montenegro"
Case C-124/95
Reference by the Court of Appeal (England and Wales) for a preliminary ruling between
The Queen
and
H.M. Treasury
and
The Bank of England
ex parte Centro-Com Srl

on the interpretation of articles 113 and 234 of the EC Treaty and Council regulation (EEC) No 1432/92 of 1 June 1992 prohibiting trade between the European Economic Community and the Republics of Serbia and Montenegro (OJ 1992 L 151, p. 4)
THE COURT hereby rules

1. The Common commercial policy provided for in article 113 of the EEC Treaty, as implemented by Council regulation (EEC) No 1432/92 of 1 June 1992 prohibiting trade between the European Economic Community and the Republics of Serbia and Montenegro and by Council regulation (EEC) No 2603/69 of 20 December 1969 establishing common rules for exports, precludes member state A from adopting, for the purpose of ensuring effective application of United Nations Security Council Resolution 757 (1992) measures prohibiting Serbian or Montenegrin funds located in its territory from being released in order to pay for goods exported by a national of member state B from that latter state to Serbia or Montenegro on the ground that member state A allows payment for such exports to be made only if the exports take place from its own territory and they have been authorized by its own competent authorities pursuant to regulation No 1432/92, when the goods in question have been classified by the Untied Nations Sanctions Committee as products intended for striclty medical purposes and the competent authorities of member state B have issued export authorizations for them in accordance with regulation No 1432/92.

2. National measures which prove to be contrary to the common commercial policy provided for in article 113 of the Treaty and to the Community regulations implementing that policy are justified under article 234 of the EEC Treaty only if they are necessary to ensure that the member state concerned performs its obligations towards non-member countries under an agreement concluded prior to entry into force of the Treaty or prior to accession by that member state.
